Thank you all for your reports. Let me summarize what we've heard and the issues we need to reconcile before I can make a final decision.

From Jonas (sustainability): Our eligible environmental project pool is exactly $18 million, matching the issuance size. From Maya (investor coverage): An anchor investor has committed to purchase its allocation only if the bond has exactly a 4-year maturity and a coupon no higher than 5.25%. This conflicts with the preliminary term sheet's 3-year maturity and 5.50% coupon.

From Victor (treasury): $10 million of the $18 million in proceeds must be allocated to refinancing debt maturing in 2027.

From Leah (legal): The bond documentation must include a make-whole redemption clause and prohibit issuer redemption during the first 12 months. The preliminary term sheet has no specified redemption protections.

So we have several conflicts with the preliminary term sheet that need to be resolved: (1) maturity -- 3 years vs. the anchor investor's 4-year requirement, (2) coupon -- 5.50% vs. the anchor investor's 5.25% cap, (3) sustainability label -- none vs. required by our green-bond framework, and (4) redemption protections -- none vs. required make-whole and 12-month no-call provisions.

Before I record terms and make the binding approval decision, I need to address these. Jonas -- if we apply the green-bond framework, we add the green label, annual allocation reporting, and external review. Maya -- can you confirm whether the anchor investor's 4-year / 5.25% terms are a hard requirement or negotiable? And does anyone see any conflict between the 4-year maturity and the $10 million 2027 refinancing allocation? I want to make sure we can reconcile all four issues in this review before I finalize.
